text:
maria: monitoring alerted: surge of kubelet network-health failures in us-west-2-azc this morning, several GPU nodes evicted pods repeatedly 
jon: saw the same, gpu-pool-3 nodes cycling between Ready and NotReady, pods OOM not the issue, network probe is flapping
sam: logs from one node show the kubelet netcheck probe failing with short tcp handshakes and ECONNRESET, could be MTU or NIC offload mismatch
lee: i've seen this pattern when jumbo frames get toggled during a kernel update rollout (GRO/LRO toggles). Are we rolling any kernel/driver changes last night?
maria: not intentionally; infra rolling kernel from 5.15.0-84 -> 5.15.0-90 in us-west-2 started at 02:10. Kernel-rollout job shows 20% completed when alerts started.
kube-health-bot: Automated probe log snippet attached: "netprobe-> to 10.0.12.1: syn, ack returned then rst within 5ms"
jon: ran iperf between two affected nodes: lots of out-of-order and small-window retransmits, MTU mismatch suspected. ip link show mtu on one node is 1500, other 9000 (why?)
sam: that explains it. GPUs are on NICs with SR-IOV, RDMA paths prefer jumbo frames. If some hosts got defaulted back to 1500 during bootstrapping we get fragmentation and short tcp resets.
lee: immediate mitigation options? We need to stop kubelet from evicting pods until we patch. Evictions are causing large job restarts and wasted GPU preempts.
maria: suggested quick fixes: 1) pause kernel rollout (rolled back the remaining batch); 2) set kubelet flag --eviction-hard to be less aggressive on network conditions? but kubelet's network eviction predicate isn't a first-class param.
jon: we can tweak node-problem-detector config or netprobe health script to be less sensitive: increase probe retry count, only mark NotReady after 3 consecutive failures instead of 1. Also add secondary check against kube-proxy health before evicting.
sam: i'm deploying a patched netcheck script to nodes in the affected ASG: it checks MTU consistency and verifies via ping -s 8972 (jumbo size) before marking network failure. Rolling that in now.
lee: for the longer term: need invariants in cluster: ensure SR-IOV RDMA hosts enforce MTU 9000 via cloud-init and validate at boot. Add an admission/controller that rejects nodes with wrong link settings.
maria: agreed. Also let's reduce eviction churn: add an admission annotation on GPU DaemonSet to delay preemption and use "eviction-soft" thresholds for pods with label gpu=true for 10s grace.
jon: quick command used to confirm mtus: `ssh node && ip -d link show eth0` and `cat /proc/net/if_inet6` (for RDMA validation). Sharing small helper script in the thread:
```
#!/bin/bash
NODE=$1
mtu_local=$(ssh $NODE ip link show eth0 | sed -n 's/.*mtu \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
echo "$NODE mtu=$mtu_local"
if [ "$mtu_local" -lt 9000 ]; then
  echo "MTU mismatch: found $mtu_local"
  exit 2
fi
```
lee: after pausing the rollout and pushing the netcheck patch, alerts dropped within 8 minutes. No further mass evictions.
maria: final action items: 1) rollback kernel batches that toggled NIC offloads (marked done), 2) push netcheck patch to all regions (sam), 3) create cluster-policy to enforce MTU on SR-IOV nodes (lee), 4) follow up to add lenient kubelet net checks to avoid single-probe evictions (jon).
sam: starting netcheck rollout umbrella job now, targeting gpu ASGs first. I'll post status when finished. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — keeping this open until next shift verifies stable for 12h. ps — cost note: each evicted GPU job requeued about 40 minutes of lost runtime; we should estimate wasted reserved capacity and add to the incident cost runbook.
jon: capturing metrics and will add cost summary to the incident doc.
lee: also created a small PR to the cloud-init templates to force `mtu: 9000` and enable `gro lro` where supported.
maria: appreciated. closing stream when postmortem doc exists."
